primitives.name: Substitution Decision Engine
primitives.verbatim_quote: I know and write down exactly how I am going to make substitutions and I think this over about as carefully as if it were our most important play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_sub': 'substitution time index', 'P_i': "player i's performance metric", 'S_{ij}': 'substitution strategy from player i to j'}
primitives.assumptions: Substitution strategies are precomputed and optimized based on expected performance gain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P_i < threshold, indicating suboptimal performance, substitution becomes mandatory but may fail due to misalignment of expectations.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's Bayesian decision tree for tactical adjustments, where each substitution is a node with probabilistic outcome weights.
layer2.telemetry: Performance metrics of substituted players and match outcome variance.

primitives.name: Pre-Arranged Seating Order
primitives.verbatim_quote: In line with this same plan, I carefully pre-arrange the seating order of the substitutes, so that those who play one position will be grouped together and under instructions to watch their particular predecessors rather than the general play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'O_p': 'ordered seating position of player p', 'P_{pred}(p)': 'preceding player in position p', 'C_p': 'cohort assignment for player p'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are assigned to positions based on role compatibility and prior performance data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When O_p ≠ P_{pred}(p), leading to confusion in substitution sequence and potential tactical misalignment.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE’s positional coordination module, where seating order determines precedence in activation and communication.
layer2.telemetry: Activation delay between substitution and actual field entry.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that effective football management hinges on deterministic planning and strategic anticipation. The temporal scheduling protocol ensures that all actions are pre-defined and synchronized with the game clock, reducing cognitive load and increasing reliability. The substitution decision engine treats each substitution as a high-stakes tactical move, requiring the same level of preparation as offensive plays. This is modeled through a Bayesian framework where prior beliefs about player performance inform posterior decisions. The pre-arranged seating order introduces a combinatorial constraint that aligns with information theory principles—specifically, minimizing entropy in communication pathways among substitutes. Failure modes arise from breakdowns in any of these components: schedule drift, poor substitution timing, or miscommunication in seating arrangements. These failures manifest as tactical inefficiencies or outright losses, as seen in the cited example of a championship lost due to a single substitution error. The system thus operates under a dual constraint: temporal precision and information integrity. Each primitive must maintain coherence across layers to ensure robustness against adversarial perturbations.
